title: Questioning before the proconsul
english: While the proconsul was holding court at Pergamum, the blessed Carpus and Papylus, witnesses of Christ, were brought into his presence. Once the proconsul had taken his seat on the tribunal, he asked, What is your name? The blessed man answered, My first and choicest name is Christian, but if you want the name I bear in the world, it is Carpus. The proconsul said, You surely know the decrees of the emperors, that you must worship the gods who govern all things, and so I urge you to step forward and offer sacrifice.

title: Refusal to sacrifice to idols
english: Carpus said: I am a Christian. I revere Christ, the Son of God, who came in the last times for our salvation and rescued us from the deception of the devil, but to such idols I offer no sacrifice. For it is impossible for me to sacrifice to the counterfeit apparitions of demons, since those who sacrifice to them become like them (Psalm 115:8). For just as the true worshippers, according to the Lord's own divine reminder, who worship God in spirit and in truth (John 4:23-24), are made like the glory of God and live deathless with him, because they have partaken of eternal life through the Word, so also those who serve these idols are made like the emptiness of the demons and perish with them in Gehenna. For it is a just sentence to share the end of the one who led astray man, the choice creature of God — I mean the devil — who by his own wickedness incited the demons to this. Know therefore, proconsul, that I do not sacrifice to these things.

title: The living do not sacrifice to the dead
english: But the proconsul, enraged, said, “Sacrifice to the gods and stop playing the fool.” Carpus, smiling faintly, said, “May the gods who did not make heaven and earth perish (Jeremiah 10:11).” The proconsul said, “You must be beaten with rods, for the emperor has so commanded.” Carpus said, “The living do not sacrifice to the dead.” The proconsul said, “Do the gods seem to you to be dead?” Carpus said, “Do you want to hear? They never lived as human beings — that they should die as well!”.

title: Idols Are Nothing Without Your Honor
english: If you would learn that this is true, strip your reverence away from them, the reverence you imagine you render them, and you will see that they are nothing, mere earthly stuff wasting away with time. For our God is beyond time and made the ages themselves, and he abides imperishable and everlasting, ever the same, accepting neither growth nor lessening, while these gods both are fashioned by human hands and rot, as I have said, under time.

Do not marvel that they utter oracles and cheat men, for the devil, fallen from the beginning out of his glorious station through his own depravity, labors to undo God's love for man, and when the saints press him hard he fights back against them, staging wars in advance and telling his own beforehand what is coming. In the same way, from what befalls us day by day, since he is older than this present order, he tests what is likely to happen and predicts it, the very evils he himself means to inflict. For from God's sentence he has both his wrongdoing and his knowing, and he tempts man only by God's leave, seeking to seduce him from true worship. Trust me then, O consular, that you stand in no small futility.

title: Babbling into blasphemy and refusal to sacrifice
english: The proconsul said, “I have let you chatter on at length, and led you into reviling the gods and the Augusti. So, lest you go still further, will you sacrifice? What do you say?” Carpus said, “I cannot sacrifice, for I have never sacrificed to idols.” At once, therefore, he ordered him to be hung up and scraped. But he kept saying, “I am a Christian.” After crying out for a long time, he grew exhausted and was no longer able to speak.

Then the proconsul left Carpus aside and turned to Papylus, saying to him, “Are you a councillor?” And he replied, “I am a citizen.” The proconsul said, “A citizen of what people?” Papylus said, “Of Thyatira.” The proconsul asked him whether he had children.
